**7B.7 Sheikh Hasina (2024)**
**Bottom line:** strongly negative. The 2024 record shows repeated use of state power to suppress scrutiny, intensify opacity, and chill critics. The main counterevidence is post-collapse accountability activity after Hasina fled on August 5, 2024, not tolerance while she still controlled the state.

**Accepted claims**
- **Bangladesh repression, security-force abuses discredit elections** | **Human Rights Watch** | **January 11, 2024** | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/bangladesh-repression-security-force-abuses-discredit-elections) | HRW reported arrests for criticism, repression of opposition, and widespread abuse before the January vote. This is early 2024 evidence that the regime was already punishing critics and shrinking space for investigators, media, and whistleblowers. | **QIDs:** `7B.7`, `7B.6`
- **Bangladesh army enforces curfew as student-led protests spiral** | **Reuters** | **July 20, 2024** | [URL](https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-army-enforces-curfew-as-student-led-protests-spiral/2182818/) | Reuters described internet/text shutdowns, curfew, roadblocks, and troop deployment during the protest crackdown. This is direct evidence of state power being used to suppress scrutiny and control the information environment. | **QIDs:** `7B.7`, `1B.8`, `7B.6`
- **Bangladesh crackdown left more than 170 dead, UN says** | **UN OHCHR** | **July 26, 2024** | [URL](https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights) | The UN said internet shutdowns increase impunity and called for impartial investigation. That strongly supports the view that Hasina’s government was not tolerating independent scrutiny of its own conduct while the crisis was unfolding. | **QIDs:** `7B.7`, `7B.6`, `7B.5`
- **Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina blames opposition for violence, curfew to remain** | **Reuters** | **July 22, 2024** | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-pm-hasina-blames-opposition-for-violence-curfew-to-remain-3528153) | Hasina kept the curfew in place and blamed political opponents for the violence. This reads as blame-shifting and defensive narrative management rather than transparency or accountability. | **QIDs:** `7B.7`, `7B.6`, `1B.8`
- **Exclusive: Bangladesh army refused to suppress protest, sealing Hasina’s fate** | **Reuters** | **August 6, 2024** | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/exclusivebangladesh-army-refused-to-suppress-protest-sealing-hasinas-fate-3558302) | Reuters reported the army would not fire on civilians to enforce Hasina’s curfew. This implies the regime was willing to rely on lethal coercion, which weighs strongly against non-accountable or restrained governance. | **QIDs:** `7B.7`, `7B.6`, `1B.5`
- **Bangladesh’s internet shutdown isolates citizens, disrupts business** | **Reuters** | **July 26, 2024** | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladeshs-internet-shutdown-isolates-citizens-disrupts-business-3539448) | Reuters said the government imposed a comprehensive internet blackout during the crisis, cutting off citizens and business activity. That is strong evidence of using state control to suppress scrutiny and conceal events in real time. | **QIDs:** `7B.7`, `7B.6`
- **Bangladesh: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report** | **Freedom House** | **2024** | [URL](https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House said anticorruption enforcement was politicized, institutions were co-opted, and the ruling party used state resources coercively. This supports the conclusion that independent oversight was not protected. | **QIDs:** `7B.7`, `7B.6`, `7B.5`
- **Bangladesh: Freedom on the Net 2024** | **Freedom House** | **2024** | [URL](https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-net/2024) | Freedom House reported manipulation of the online information environment, blocking major news sites, and throttling communications around BNP rallies and later unrest. This is direct evidence of censorship-like control that would impede whistleblowers and investigators. | **QIDs:** `7B.7`, `7B.6`, `7B.5`

**Limited counterevidence**
- **Former Bangladesh PM Hasina demands probe into July ‘killings and vandalism’** | **Reuters** | **August 13, 2024** | [URL](https://theprint.in/world/former-bangladesh-pm-hasina-demands-probe-into-july-killings-and-vandalism/2222256/) | This is the closest pro-accountability signal, but it came after Hasina fled the country. It does not show she tolerated investigation while still in office. | **QIDs:** `7B.7`, `7B.6`
- **Bangladesh court orders probe into former PM Hasina’s role in grocer’s death** | **Reuters** | **August 13, 2024** | [URL](https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-court-orders-probe-into-former-pm-hasinas-role-in-grocers-death/2221579/) | A court-initiated probe is evidence that independent inquiry became possible only after her exit. It is counterevidence to absolute impunity, but not evidence that Hasina allowed scrutiny in power. | **QIDs:** `7B.7`, `7B.6`
- **ACC begins probe into graft allegations against Hasina, family members** | **BSS** | **December 17, 2024** | [URL](https://www.bssnews.net/news/231568) | The ACC opened probes into alleged embezzlement involving Hasina and family members. This is meaningful accountability activity, but it happened after regime collapse, so it does not show tolerance of independent scrutiny in office. | **QIDs:** `7B.7`, `7B.6`
- **Graft allegations: ACC seeks info on Hasina, family from CA’s office, govt agencies** | **The Daily Star** | **December 24, 2024** | [URL](https://www.thedailystar.net/news/corruption/news/graft-allegations-acc-seeks-info-hasina-family-cas-office-govt-agencies-3783716) | The ACC sought records from state bodies to investigate Hasina and her family over alleged abuses and irregularities. Again, this is post-ouster scrutiny, not evidence of tolerance while she governed. | **QIDs:** `7B.7`, `7B.6`

**Search gap**
- I did not find a reliable 2024 source showing Hasina’s government voluntarily protected investigators, auditors, prosecutors, courts, media, or whistleblowers while she still held power.
- The strongest affirmative evidence is post-August-5 accountability activity, which is evidence of delayed scrutiny after collapse, not tolerance in office.
- I also did not find a credible source that clearly documented a transparent internal audit or disclosure process reaching Hasina’s own conduct, assets, or concealed decisions during 2024.
